## Summary

Define CFEL

## Claim

### Formal Claim

```CFEL
p{:occurrence}: [value format]{:value count};
p.*[name format]{:immediate name count};
p.**[name format]{:recursive name count};
p.*[name format]{:immediate name count}: [value format]{:value count}
```

### Prose Claim

CFEL (CAPRMEDIO Formal Expression Language) is the formal notation for
Subject addresses and fenced Formal Claims. CFEL is a model component beside
Graph and Carrier: Graph contains Nodes and Relations; CFEL addresses and
constrains them. CFEL syntax neither creates a Node, Relation, Property,
Carrier fact, Workflow step, nor evaluator result.

CFEL uses these graph-address forms:

- `X/Y` selects a narrower Primary Node; `X//Name` selects an existing
  instance of a Primary Node.
- `X.p` addresses Property p borne by X. In a Subject only,
  `X/(.p := V)` combines an admitted Property value with selection of X;
  `:=` is not a Formal-Claim value assignment.
- `Part +> Whole` and `Whole <+ Part` are opposite written views of one
  containment fact. `X >| Axis` and `Axis |< X` are opposite written views
  of one classification fact. A bare qualified address references its declared entity or instance. No `@` reference operator is required; `@N` identity/version tags retain their separate meaning.
- Parentheses group one expression. `;` separates complete expressions;
  a line break has no conjunction or disjunction meaning.

In Formal Claims, `X: Y` admits Y as an allowed value of X regardless of X's
kind or preceding path; it is not assignment. `=` and `!=` test conditions,
and `==` states a required or derived conclusion. `in` and `not in` are the
admitted membership tests. Numeric comparison and addition use the separately
defined `>`, `>=`, `<`, `<=` and `+`; they are distinct from Relation
operators. Property occurrence, direct-value, immediate-name
and recursive-name counts are distinct:

`{:n}`, `{:n+}` and `{:n..m}` state allowed cardinality bounds on their
qualified selection; `{=n}` tests a count condition, `{>n}` tests whether the
actual count is greater than n using the existing numeric `>`, and `{==n}`
concludes a required or derived count. These test/conclusion forms are not
allowed bounds. A Relation has independent outgoing and
reverse cardinalities: `Source {:forward}((RELATION)){:reverse} Target`.
Omitted annotations are unspecified, not zero. `[format]` applies to direct
values; a name selector is not a value selector. A `p.**` count aggregates
selected distinct descendant Property identities below p within each selected
bearer, independently of direct values and other bearers.

The following named constructs are admitted only with the semantics in their
own CFEL Rules: `IF`/`THEN`, `UNIQUE`, `DETERMINES`, `COUNT`, `MAX`,
`LOOKUP`, `FENCED_LABELS`, and `?=`. `>>` is delivery notation with the
semantics of the delivery Rule; `!(selectors)` excludes branches from a
delivery selection. `Kind//$x` binds an existing selected instance and `$x.p`
reads its Property. Each non-graph CFEL operator has its own Declaration;
an operator is not a binary Node Relation. A Requirement/Declaration describes
a canonical or derived Relation direction; it does not authorize a second
stored inverse fact.

The reusable metadata family `Operator//Name == "notation literal"` binds a
declared operator descriptor to its token or bounded construct spelling. Its
quoted right side is metadata, not an executed CFEL expression, value assignment,
state creation, or a new model entity.

A direct Relation Declaration owns shared meaning and endpoints. A derived Declaration retains the reverse counterpart binding and its own alias, when present. `alias(Relation//NAME) == "token"` binds exact Relation names to lexical notation. `Relation//DIRECT <--> Relation//DERIVED` binds distinct inverse Relations in the direct Declaration. It never equates their identities. These metadata forms do not create literal-to-Node graph links.

A graph Relation connects declared model entities or declared instances,
including Carrier and CFEL; it is not limited to `Node/**`. A literal remains a
Property or allowed value, not a graph endpoint. A non-graph CFEL operator is
not itself a graph Relation, but its declared operator descriptor is a model
entity that may be a graph endpoint; an operator glyph or literal operand does
not create another model entity. Each direct Relation Declaration supplies shared meaning and a
formal Host/Target signature with typed selectors whose universe is known, or
with declared variables bound to that universe. Within a Relation Declaration
Formal Claim only, `$host ((RELATION)) $target` is the reusable generic
signature: its untyped variables range over that declared entity-or-instance
universe and exclude literals. It declares neither a Relation fact nor instance
data. Known endpoint kinds remain typed selectors. This binding applies within Relation Declarations.

Concrete directional alternatives describe the same canonical Relation fact:
`Step ((IS_CONTAINED_BY)) Workflow` and
`Workflow <((IS_CONTAINED_BY)) Step`. The bare forward form
`Step ((IS_CONTAINED_BY)) Workflow` remains valid. In reverse writing,
normalization swaps canonical Source/Target and the two written endpoint count
slots. This syntax does not grant an inverse Relation permission. The Relation Declaration states the Host, Target and counterpart direction. `HAS_INVERSE` remains distinct from the confirmed
canonical-Relation-versus-derived-view policy; this Definition does not
introduce a placeholder Relation, metadata Node, or evaluator.

In RMED Claims, all formal content is a fenced block labelled `CFEL`. CFEL
body syntax and Markdown-fence-label parsing are separate concerns. This Definition
describes the admitted language contract; it does not claim a complete parser
or evaluator. An unimplemented construct remains an adoption and conformance
gap, not evidence that the construct has different semantics.

This Definition does not convert a Format, Bool value, or any other value
into an instance selected by `//`. Such an instance selection requires the
existing source binding that declares it. No value-format-to-instance rewrite
is implied by the CFEL overview.

Define Cardinality


remain in their governing Declarations.

## Summary

Define Value Format

## Claim

### Formal Claim

```CFEL
CFEL <+ Format;
Format.Data Type{:1}: [string]{:1};
Format.Data Type.*[]{:0};
Format.Uniqueness Selection{:0..1}: [string]{:1};
Format.Uniqueness Selection.*[]{:0}
```

### Prose Claim


Format defines the admissible value domain of each direct Property value,
separately from its cardinality. In CFEL, `Format` is the language element for
expressing that value domain. Data Type names the value domain. Uniqueness
Selection names the comparison population. List and map are Carrier
structures, not Value Formats. A YAML sequence carries multiple values, and a
mapping carries dependent Properties. `ref` is not a Value Format. Identifying
values use the `string` Format; their Definition identifies the referenced
object. Nested Properties have independent Formats and cardinalities. YAML
null and an empty string each count as one direct value when present; Format
and prose conditions determine admissibility.



## Semantics

Format annotations constrain direct values. Markdown, YAML, TOML and JSON are
Carrier representation formats, not value Formats. The initial scalar
vocabulary—bool, datetime, decimal, float, int and string—is provisional. A
format annotation selects a value domain; it does not impose uniqueness.

## Details

Formula expressions, function-style uniqueness notation and bracketed
conditions remain separate proposals.

Define scalar Value Format

### Formal Claim

```CFEL
CFEL <+ Format/scalar
```

The scalar Value Format admits a direct primitive value, including string,
numeric, Boolean, date/time and null values supported by the declared Carrier.

individually, while child mapping keys are not direct values of their parent.

specifications govern concrete result shapes; no function or advanced
condition syntax is introduced.

## Summary

Define Relation

## Claim

### Formal Claim

```CFEL
Relation.Name{:1}: [string]{:1};
Relation.Name.*[]{:0};
Relation.Meaning{:1}: [string]{:1};
Relation.Meaning.*[]{:0}
```

### Prose Claim

Relation defines a reusable directed graph Relation Type with a Name and Meaning. Each actual link is a tuple (Host, Relation Type, Target); persist each direct fact once. Endpoints are declared model Entities or instances, including Carrier and CFEL descriptors, and exclude literal values and glyphs. An operator is distinct from a graph Relation even when its notation spells a Relation traversal. Its declared descriptor may be an endpoint.

A direct Relation Declaration owns shared meaning, endpoint signature and any counterpart binding. A derived counterpart remains a distinct Relation with its own Declaration; its meaning and endpoints are inferred through that binding. An alias supplies lexical notation for one Relation; it does not create a new Relation, a Node or a separate Relation ID.

## Summary

Define Term

## Claim

### Prose Claim


Project-specific vocabulary used as reusable lexical components of complete or qualified entity names and authored content, including the word `Term` itself.


A Term is a direct specialization of Entity at `Term`. A Term has one Name, the word or phrase used for its meaning. Its named instances initially form a flat set, using `Term//<Name>` without additional Term groups. This declares the vocabulary kind and its existing Name property; it does not implement the deferred Terms Graph.

**every** instance of `Term` **must** represent a reusable word **or** phrase component of complete **or** qualified entity expressions **and** authored content whose approved Project-specific meaning remains consistent across **all** its uses.


```text
Term
Term.Name[string]{1}
```

## Details

This Requirement Atom of Type Entity Definition defines the kind at `Term` and its Name property. Its Claim states membership and structural constraints; the separate proposed Method Term Definition owns the word Term's lexical meaning at `Term//Term`. That Method Draft explicitly introduces the lexical instance. This structural Requirement does not supply its dedicated Method ownership or prove its admission under CA-R-1319. Using the word Term in its own definition does not require another lexical instance or an infinite chain of definition layers.

The lexical forms `Package`, `Eval Package` and `Runtime Package` illustrate reuse of the Term `Package`; `Scope Unit` and `Code Unit` illustrate reuse of the Term `Unit`. These lexical forms are not asserted to be complete canonical entity names outside the Term branch. An Entity outside the Term branch uses its complete source-admitted expression as its canonical name. Its complete name cannot be just one registered Term; the sole exception is `Entity`, because it is the Subject root. Reusable Terms occur as components within qualified expressions. Reusing `Package` inside `Eval Package` does not itself reference the separately named `Package` entity or establish a Relation. Lexical composition does not introduce another entity or require a separate `Unit` instance.

The earlier schematic example `Package > Module > Code Unit` connects three entities; its short displayed labels do not by themselves establish their full canonical names. Authored references use the complete source-admitted expressions for those entities. The contextual topic/code spellings `atom.id` and `projection.id` distinguish their respective ID Properties; they are not alternative complete canonical Subject names or case-folded aliases. Authored Subjects use their full admitted expressions. These spellings reuse the Term `ID`; their shared terminal label is not a collision. The dot remains an operator. Neither spelling is replaced with `atom.atom_id` or another invented spelling. Arbitrary composite expressions are not one Term under CA-R-1325 or automatically one entity name. Literal source quotations and code identifiers are distinguished from authored entity mentions and are not automatically renamed.

A Governed Term has exactly one dedicated active Method Atom of Type Term Definition as its authoritative meaning owner under the proposed successor of CA-R-1319 and the new Method-qualified Type declaration. The lexical Term target is distinct from an entity whose complete name uses it. A defining Atom may explicitly introduce its lexical target under CA-R-1194 and CA-R-1931; a parser or word occurrence does not introduce it. The confirmed placement supplies direct lexical targets such as `Term//Empty` and `Term//ID`; these examples do not generate their lexical definitions or establish those instances without the respective defining Claims. No dictionary Projection, extractor, lookup, Term groups, or Terms Graph implementation is required.

The only Entity outside the Term branch whose complete canonical name is also a registered Term is `Entity`, because it is the Subject root. The R / Entity Definition governs `Entity`; the M / Term Definition governs `Term//Entity`. Their matching word does not merge the two targets. Root status in another hierarchy does not extend this sole Subject-root exception.

Use the full expression when identifying or comparing entities. `Atom/(.Header.Role: X)/(.Header.Form: X)` is a possible qualified expression: the repeated X components retain the same Term meaning while their complete qualifications differ. Each value still requires admission in its own context; the example does not introduce X or new value admissions. Likewise, `Entity/Property` is a qualified entity expression, while Property is the lexical Term at `Term//Property`. This distinction does not withdraw either pending definition or require a new Term Definition for every complete entity expression.

### Draft source pin

## Summary

Define Term

## Claim

### Prose Claim


Project-specific vocabulary used as reusable lexical components of complete or qualified entity names and authored content, including the word `Term` itself.


A Term is a direct specialization of Entity at `Term`. A Term has one Name, the word or phrase used for its meaning. Its named instances initially form a flat set, using `Term//<Name>` without additional Term groups. This declares the vocabulary kind and its existing Name property; it does not implement the deferred Terms Graph.

**every** instance of `Term` **must** represent a reusable word **or** phrase component of complete **or** qualified entity expressions **and** authored content whose approved Project-specific meaning remains consistent across **all** its uses.


```text
Term
Term.Name[string]{1}
```

## Details

This Requirement Atom of Type Entity Definition defines the kind at `Term` and its Name property. Its Claim states membership and structural constraints; the separate proposed Method Term Definition owns the word Term's lexical meaning at `Term//Term`. That Method Draft explicitly introduces the lexical instance. This structural Requirement does not supply its dedicated Method ownership or prove its admission under CA-R-1319. Using the word Term in its own definition does not require another lexical instance or an infinite chain of definition layers.

The lexical forms `Package`, `Eval Package` and `Runtime Package` illustrate reuse of the Term `Package`; `Scope Unit` and `Code Unit` illustrate reuse of the Term `Unit`. These lexical forms are not asserted to be complete canonical entity names outside the Term branch. An Entity outside the Term branch uses its complete source-admitted expression as its canonical name. Its complete name cannot be just one registered Term; the sole exception is `Entity`, because it is the Subject root. Reusable Terms occur as components within qualified expressions. Reusing `Package` inside `Eval Package` does not itself reference the separately named `Package` entity or establish a Relation. Lexical composition does not introduce another entity or require a separate `Unit` instance.

The earlier schematic example `Package > Module > Code Unit` connects three entities; its short displayed labels do not by themselves establish their full canonical names. Authored references use the complete source-admitted expressions for those entities. The contextual topic/code spellings `atom.id` and `projection.id` distinguish their respective ID Properties; they are not alternative complete canonical Subject names or case-folded aliases. Authored Subjects use their full admitted expressions. These spellings reuse the Term `ID`; their shared terminal label is not a collision. The dot remains an operator. Neither spelling is replaced with `atom.atom_id` or another invented spelling. Arbitrary composite expressions are not one Term under CA-R-1325 or automatically one entity name. Literal source quotations and code identifiers are distinguished from authored entity mentions and are not automatically renamed.

A Governed Term has exactly one dedicated active Method Atom of Type Term Definition as its authoritative meaning owner under the proposed successor of CA-R-1319 and the new Method-qualified Type declaration. The lexical Term target is distinct from an entity whose complete name uses it. A defining Atom may explicitly introduce its lexical target under CA-R-1194 and CA-R-1931; a parser or word occurrence does not introduce it. The confirmed placement supplies direct lexical targets such as `Term//Empty` and `Term//ID`; these examples do not generate their lexical definitions or establish those instances without the respective defining Claims. No dictionary Projection, extractor, lookup, Term groups, or Terms Graph implementation is required.

The only Entity outside the Term branch whose complete canonical name is also a registered Term is `Entity`, because it is the Subject root. The R / Entity Definition governs `Entity`; the M / Term Definition governs `Term//Entity`. Their matching word does not merge the two targets. Root status in another hierarchy does not extend this sole Subject-root exception.

Use the full expression when identifying or comparing entities. `Atom/(.Header.Role: X)/(.Header.Form: X)` is a possible qualified expression: the repeated X components retain the same Term meaning while their complete qualifications differ. Each value still requires admission in its own context; the example does not introduce X or new value admissions. Likewise, `Entity/Property` is a qualified entity expression, while Property is the lexical Term at `Term//Property`. This distinction does not withdraw either pending definition or require a new Term Definition for every complete entity expression.


### Prose Claim

A Term is a reusable word or phrase component of entity expressions and authored content. Its Project-specific meaning remains consistent across uses and is owned by its active Method/Form Term Definition. Vocabulary Terms are lexical items, not graph Nodes merely because they are used as words. A Term has one Name.

## Semantics

A Term provides a reusable word or phrase; its full context supplies the expression in which it appears.

## Summary

Declare Relation endpoints

## Claim

### Prose Claim

Each graph Relation, direct or derived, has exactly one Requirement / Declaration in the selected effective MODEL. A direct Relation Declaration owns its shared meaning, allowed Host and Target signature, endpoint conditions, Direct classification and each declared inverse/counterpart binding. Each derived Relation retains its own Declaration. Infer its reversed endpoints, meaning, Derived classification and source binding from the direct Declaration; do not duplicate them on the derived side. Its Formal Claim contains the reverse written view of its counterpart binding and its own lexical alias when one exists. Relation-object endpoints use qualified addresses `Relation//NAME`; the middle `((HAS_INVERSE))` is the graph Relation operator. An endpoint reference does not execute that Relation as an operator.

A Relation endpoint is a declared model Entity or declared instance, including Carrier and CFEL descriptors. Literal values and operator glyphs are not graph endpoints. Untyped endpoint-signature variables range over this declared entity-or-instance universe and exclude literals. Typed selectors retain their declared populations and conditions. A signature constrains admissible links; it does not create links. An unresolved endpoint population is a diagnostic, not proof of an empty or valid signature. NARROWER_THAN is restricted to MODEL kinds; this rule introduces no further cross-layer endpoint restriction.

`alias(Relation//RELATION_NAME) == "token"` binds one declared Relation's exact name to one nonempty notation token. It is lexical metadata, not a graph Relation between a literal and a Node, and does not equate Relation identities. A Relation has at most one authored alias. No alias means full named notation. Resolve names exactly; case folding and undeclared name synonyms are not admitted. Reject unknown names, conflicting aliases and ambiguous token bindings in the selected effective MODEL. Directional reading follows the owning Declaration; an alias does not authorize a new direction.

The direct Declaration records `Relation//DIRECT ((HAS_INVERSE)) Relation//DERIVED`, equivalently `Relation//DIRECT <--> Relation//DERIVED`. A no-alias derived Declaration records `Relation//DERIVED <((HAS_INVERSE)) Relation//DIRECT`, the reverse written view of that same binding fact. Each side names a distinct declared Relation. After normalizing written direction, the canonical Host is the direct source and the canonical Target is its derived inverse. Infer inverse links only from admitted direct facts by swapping endpoints. Reject a self-pair, multiple direct sources for one inverse, a derived canonical Host and conflicting counterpart bindings. A qualified counterpart retains the qualification at its direct source and is derived only from matching facts.

`Host ((R)) Target` is the named forward view. `Target <((R)) Host` is reverse writing of that same fact. Normalize endpoint counts with the written endpoints. Neither reverse writing nor an inverse binding grants permission, cardinality or a second authored fact. Each direction still needs its own applicable outgoing permission and bounds. Matching and counting use exact Host, Relation, Target and model/instance selectors.

## Summary

Define Artifact

## Claim

### Prose Claim


The reusable lexical Term Artifact in model statements about Entity instances
and their Carrier representations.


Artifact **means** an Entity instance represented in a Carrier. This Claim
explicitly introduces the lexical Term instance Artifact at
`Term//Artifact`.

## Semantics

A file, folder or database row can serve as a Carrier. The Term refers to the
Entity instance, not its Carrier. An Entity retains its
identity when referred to as an Artifact, including where more than one
Carrier represents it. Artifact does not declare another Entity kind,
classification axis, Property, or second identity.

Entity admission remains governed by the pending Entity Definition; Carrier
binding remains governed by CARRIES. This lexical Definition adds neither
admission policy nor Carrier-binding policy.

## Details

The Operator states that Artifact is a Term for Entity instances represented
in Carriers. This supersedes the proposed new Artifact classification. The
role-only marker allocates no canonical Method identity.

Current R1994@14 is historical evidence for this Draft package and is planned
for future Retirement after its Entity constraints move to the Entity
Definition. It remains Current until coordinated retirement; in the proposed owner
structure it will not own the lexical Artifact meaning.

## Summary

Define Markdown and YAML regions in a File Carrier

## Claim

### Prose Claim


For a Markdown File Carrier, Main Content is its Markdown body and YAML Frontmatter is its optional structured metadata region. Main Content can contain Paragraphs and CCE Operator occurrences; these are content parts, not additional Files. A Frontmatter Scalar is one direct primitive value within a declared metadata field. These logical regions are not separate Carriers.

The Filename may contain zero or more Scope Unit Tokens. Each serialized Scope Unit reference uses one token under CA-D-302; this does not require all File names to carry such a token.


```text
Carrier/File.Main Content[string]{0..1}
Carrier/File.Main Content.Paragraph[string]{0+}
Carrier/File.Main Content.CCE Operator[string]{0+}
Carrier/File.YAML Frontmatter{0}
Carrier/File.YAML Frontmatter.Scalar[scalar]{0+}
Carrier/File.Filename.Scope Unit Token[string]{0+}
```

## Details

The declared File format and applicable D Policy determine required regions, tokens and actual encoding. Complete RMED Atom Markdown still requires its Summary and Claim. This definition adds no section, field, token or file to those policies.

## Summary

Define Markdown File Carrier

## Claim

### Prose Claim


Markdown File Carriers and their File-Carrier Format.


A Markdown File Carrier **means** a File Carrier whose Format is Markdown.


```text
Carrier/File/Markdown
```

## Semantics

`Carrier/File/Markdown` is an Entity kind. Its `/` path expresses
specialization and inheritance from `Carrier/File`; it is not a lexical
Term hierarchy. Names in the path may reuse lexical Terms. The existing File Carrier definition
supplies inherited File-Carrier structure, while the registered Markdown
Format supplies Markdown encoding and interpretation rules.

YAML Frontmatter is optional for a Markdown File Carrier under the existing
File-region Rule. This definition therefore does not require YAML Frontmatter
for every Markdown file. It does not define a filename, extension, identifier,
section, field, lifecycle, or a separate Carrier for a Markdown region.

## Details

This role-only Draft defines one new structural target and allocates no
canonical Requirement identity. It does not automatically introduce a lexical
Term or a Method Term Definition. The more specific Markdown Atom Carrier kind
is a separate target with separate defining authority.

## Summary

Validate CCE lexical case

## Claim

### Prose Claim

CCE Claims evaluated for lexical case and Markdown operator representation.


**Claim checked.**

**every** CCE Claim satisfies the lexical-case Method CA-M-229-CORE_META_MODEL-IMPLEMENTATION_METHOD--render-governed-terms-and-cce-operators-distinctly **and** the Markdown operator representation specified by CA-D-280-CORE_META_MODEL-ENG_DECISION--serialize-cce-operators-in-bold.

## Details

### Test case

- identify the tested CCE version, applicable CCE Operator Registry under CA-M-234-CORE_META_MODEL-IMPLEMENTATION_METHOD--register-expandable-canonical-cce-operator-list, **and** exact Revisions of the checked authority. record the fixtures **and** their expected results.
- create valid fixtures with ordinary English words at sentence **and** list-item starts. include ordinary words that are **not** named Terms.
- create valid fixtures beginning with a Governed Term, a General Term, an exact Scope Unit Name, **and** an exact registered reference. preserve the case required for the token rather than changing it because of its sentence **or** list position.
- use **every** registered word-form CCE Operator **in** a valid context at sentence-initial **and** sentence-internal positions **where** the applicable grammar admits that position. include whole multiword forms such as **must not**, **not in**, **is not empty**, **starts with**, **and** **ends with**.
- use **every** registered symbolic CCE Operator **in** a valid context with the representation required by CA-D-280. include **`=`**, **`!=`**, **`<`**, **`<=`**, **`>`**, **`>=`**, **and** cardinality forms such as **`=1`** **and** **`>=1`**.
- derive invalid fixtures by applying **`=1`** of these mutations at a time:
  - capitalize an ordinary sentence-initial word.
  - capitalize an ordinary list-initial word.
  - capitalize a word-form CCE Operator.
  - remove an emphasis delimiter pair.
  - add an unmatched emphasis delimiter.
  - emphasize **only** part of a multiword CCE Operator.
  - omit bold rendering from a symbolic CCE Operator.
  - retain bold rendering but remove its inline-code rendering.
  - lowercase a Governed Term.
  - capitalize a General Term.
  - alter an exact Scope Unit Name.
  - alter an exact registered reference.

### Acceptance criteria

- **every** valid fixture retains **`=1`** precise interpretation **and** passes the lexical-case **and** representation checks.
- **every** invalid fixture fails the affected check. the result identifies the incorrect token occurrence, actual representation, expected token class **and** representation, **and** checked authority.
- fixture expectations come from the checked authority; this Evaluation **must not** introduce another operator spelling **or** formatting rule.

### Failure disposition

record a Concern naming the affected CCE Claim **and** incorrect token. checking **must not** rewrite the source Claim.

## Summary

Validate CCE lexical case

## Claim

### Prose Claim

CCE Claims evaluated for lexical case and Markdown operator representation.


**Claim checked.**

**every** CCE Claim satisfies the lexical-case Method CA-M-229-CORE_META_MODEL-IMPLEMENTATION_METHOD--render-governed-terms-and-cce-operators-distinctly **and** the Markdown operator representation specified by CA-D-280-CORE_META_MODEL-ENG_DECISION--serialize-cce-operators-in-bold.

## Details

### Test case

- identify the tested CCE version, applicable CCE Operator Registry under CA-M-234-CORE_META_MODEL-IMPLEMENTATION_METHOD--register-expandable-canonical-cce-operator-list, **and** exact Revisions of the checked authority. record the fixtures **and** their expected results.
- create valid fixtures with ordinary English words at sentence **and** list-item starts. include ordinary words that are **not** named Terms.
- create valid fixtures beginning with a Governed Term, a General Term, an exact Scope Unit Name, **and** an exact registered reference. preserve the case required for the token rather than changing it because of its sentence **or** list position.
- use **every** registered word-form CCE Operator **in** a valid context at sentence-initial **and** sentence-internal positions **where** the applicable grammar admits that position. include whole multiword forms such as **must not**, **not in**, **is not empty**, **starts with**, **and** **ends with**.
- use **every** registered symbolic CCE Operator **in** a valid context with the representation required by CA-D-280. include **`=`**, **`!=`**, **`<`**, **`<=`**, **`>`**, **`>=`**, **and** cardinality forms such as **`=1`** **and** **`>=1`**.
- derive invalid fixtures by applying **`=1`** of these mutations at a time:
  - capitalize an ordinary sentence-initial word.
  - capitalize an ordinary list-initial word.
  - capitalize a word-form CCE Operator.
  - remove an emphasis delimiter pair.
  - add an unmatched emphasis delimiter.
  - emphasize **only** part of a multiword CCE Operator.
  - omit bold rendering from a symbolic CCE Operator.
  - retain bold rendering but remove its inline-code rendering.
  - lowercase a Governed Term.
  - capitalize a General Term.
  - alter an exact Scope Unit Name.
  - alter an exact registered reference.

### Acceptance criteria

- **every** valid fixture retains **`=1`** precise interpretation **and** passes the lexical-case **and** representation checks.
- **every** invalid fixture fails the affected check. the result identifies the incorrect token occurrence, actual representation, expected token class **and** representation, **and** checked authority.
- fixture expectations come from the checked authority; this Evaluation **must not** introduce another operator spelling **or** formatting rule.

### Failure disposition

record a Concern naming the affected CCE Claim **and** incorrect token. checking **must not** rewrite the source Claim.

## Summary

Refresh Updated At whenever an Atom changes

## Claim

### Prose Claim


accepted Markdown Atom Carrier edits.


**every** actual accepted edit **to** an Atom Carrier **must** refresh that Current Atom's `updated_at` **to** the actual Project-time edit instant, including a formatting, lossless serialization, Entity-name, admitted Current Status, direct-owner, **or** current-Atom local-placement edit. an exact no-op **must** retain Updated At. When a real update publishes a successor and archives its predecessor, the Archive Carrier **must** retain the predecessor's prior Updated At, numeric Version, and unrelated content while carrying the Archived status and version-qualified identity; Git history preserves the exact pre-archive bytes. Standalone archival is not an edit to the Current Atom's content: it only materializes the Archived representation with its version-qualified identity, filename and location, so it does not create a successor or refresh Updated At.

## Details

an ancestor-only move that changes an Atom's repository locator **without** changing its own bytes, metadata, direct owner **or** placement relative **to** that owner is **not** an edit **to** that Atom. retain its Updated At **and** Version under CA-R-1432. this applies **to** **every** Atom, regardless of Content Role; it does **not** exempt an actual Status, filename, ownership **or** local-placement change. Git history retains exact pre-archive bytes.

changing a Current Atom's Status **and** publishing a Current successor is an actual update governed by CA-R-1432: archive the old-version identity with unchanged numeric Version and Updated At, while the Current successor receives its incremented Version and actual edit time. A standalone transition of the Current representation to Archived follows the exception above. timestamp encoding follows `CA-D-270-CORE_META_MODEL-DELIVERY--serialize-atom-revision-metadata-in-frontmatter`.

## Summary

Refresh Updated At whenever an Atom changes

## Claim

### Prose Claim


accepted Markdown Atom Carrier edits.


**every** actual accepted edit **to** an Atom Carrier **must** refresh that Current Atom's `updated_at` **to** the actual Project-time edit instant, including a formatting, lossless serialization, Entity-name, admitted Current Status, direct-owner, **or** current-Atom local-placement edit. an exact no-op **must** retain Updated At. When a real update publishes a successor and archives its predecessor, the Archive Carrier **must** retain the predecessor's prior Updated At, numeric Version, and unrelated content while carrying the Archived status and version-qualified identity; Git history preserves the exact pre-archive bytes. Standalone archival is not an edit to the Current Atom's content: it only materializes the Archived representation with its version-qualified identity, filename and location, so it does not create a successor or refresh Updated At.

## Details

an ancestor-only move that changes an Atom's repository locator **without** changing its own bytes, metadata, direct owner **or** placement relative **to** that owner is **not** an edit **to** that Atom. retain its Updated At **and** Version under CA-R-1432. this applies **to** **every** Atom, regardless of Content Role; it does **not** exempt an actual Status, filename, ownership **or** local-placement change. Git history retains exact pre-archive bytes.

changing a Current Atom's Status **and** publishing a Current successor is an actual update governed by CA-R-1432: archive the old-version identity with unchanged numeric Version and Updated At, while the Current successor receives its incremented Version and actual edit time. A standalone transition of the Current representation to Archived follows the exception above. timestamp encoding follows `CA-D-270-CORE_META_MODEL-DELIVERY--serialize-atom-revision-metadata-in-frontmatter`.

## Summary

Repair accidental Atom ID reuse

## Claim

### Prose Claim


repair of accidental reuse of assigned Project Atom IDs.


**to** repair accidental reuse of an assigned Project Atom ID, an AI Agent **must** perform **all** of:

1. identify the distinct source Atoms by exact Carrier address, Revision, **and** recorded history. distinguish accidental reuse from legitimate Revisions of the same Atom **and** derived copies of its Carrier.
2. establish the original valid owner from recorded assignment history. **if** the original owner cannot be established at the effective Confidence Threshold, request an Operator decision for that collision **before** changing its identities **or** references. filename order, discovery order, current filesystem timestamps, **or** the highest Version **must not** select the owner.
3. preserve the original owner's Atom ID. give **every** later accidental reuse the next unreused Project-wide number for its own Content Role under CA-D-450-CORE_META_MODEL-DELIVERY--number-project-owned-atoms-within-each-content-role, using the encoding under CA-D-378-CORE_META_MODEL-DELIVERY--serialize-assigned-atom-identities. this corrects invalid reuse **and** does **not** authorize changing a valid owner's immutable identity.
4. preserve **every** affected Atom's Claim, Content Role, Atom Scope, Claim Target Scope Unit, **and** textual Claim Scope. preserve its immutable prior Revisions **and** recorded history; record the exact predecessor-to-corrected-identity mapping **in** the existing Work Journal **without** rewriting historical Carriers **or** Records.
5. resolve **every** affected current reference against its intended Atom using the reference's context **and** recorded history. update references **only** **when** their intended targets are established; request an Operator decision for unresolved references. do **not** replace the ambiguous ID indiscriminately.
6. verify that the repaired active identities resolve uniquely **and** **every** affected current reference still identifies its intended Claim **before** declaring the collision repaired. keep unrelated Claims **and** identities unchanged.
7. perform repair as an explicitly authorized source change, **not** as an automatic side effect of lookup **or** compilation. preserve CA-D-336-CORE_META_MODEL-DELIVERY--resolve-active-atoms-from-canonical-carrier-identities's failure on ambiguous lookup **until** source repair is complete, **and** regenerate affected Projections from their corrected sources through their existing governed workflows.

## Summary

Validate accidental Atom ID reuse repair

## Claim

### Prose Claim


Atom ID collision repairs.


the Evaluation **must** reject completion of an Atom ID collision repair under CA-M-276-CORE_META_MODEL-IMPLEMENTATION_METHOD--repair-accidental-atom-id-reuse **if** **any** of:

- the original owner was selected **without** sufficient recorded assignment evidence **or** the required Operator decision, **or** its valid Atom ID changed.
- a later accidental reuse retains the colliding ID, receives a previously used number, **or** receives an ID outside its Project prefix **and** Content Role sequence.
- an affected Claim, Content Role, Atom Scope, Claim Target Scope Unit, **or** textual Claim Scope changes beyond the approved identity-reference correction, a distinct Claim is lost **or** merged, **or** an unrelated identity changes.
- a prior Revision **or** historical Record is rewritten, history becomes unreachable, **or** the Work Journal lacks the exact mapping between the historical Carrier **and** its corrected identity.
- an affected current reference resolves ambiguously, remains unresolved, **or** resolves **to** a different intended Claim; an uncertain reference is rebound **without** the required Operator decision.
- legitimate same-Atom Revisions **or** derived copies are renumbered as accidental reuse, **or** lookup **or** compilation silently selects an identity winner.

the Evaluation **must** distinguish a paused collision awaiting an Operator decision from a completed repair. its checks **must** cover the verified-original-owner case, reversed Carrier discovery order, an unknown original owner, an ambiguous incoming reference, **and** legitimate same-Atom Revisions **or** derived copies.

## Summary

Validate nested Tool-call evidence

## Claim

### Prose Claim


serialized Tool-call evidence within a Step Run.


the Main Content of a Journal Carrier that encodes Tool-call evidence within a Step Run **must** undergo an actual Evaluation under CA-R-1528. Available wire evidence alone is **not** a passing result.

## Details

the Evaluation of that Main Content **must** run and report a passing, failed, or unresolved result. It **must**:

- check whether several Tool calls by an Agentic Action inside a leaf Step Run carry their actual parent Step Run, Tool identities, inputs **or** admitted protected references, results **or** errors, **and** distinguishing call evidence; report failure when required wire evidence is absent;
- check whether repeated attempts with the same Tool **and** inputs retain distinct attempt identities without claiming a second effect when its outcome is unknown; report unresolved when the supplied evidence cannot distinguish the effect;
- check whether a failed Tool call or unconfirmed effect is recorded as that outcome rather than successful completion; report failure for a contradicted success claim;
- check whether a rebuilt nested trace derives from the canonical Journal without another source of execution history; report failure when another source is claimed;
- reject an inference that a Tool call automatically creates a Workflow Step, a Conditional Step route, **or** a new Action definition; and
- check whether secret input uses a governed protected representation rather than plaintext duplication; report failure when plaintext is present.

the Evaluation **must not** edit supplied wire evidence. Missing wire evidence **or** an unperformed Evaluation is **not** a passing result.

- check whether several Tool calls by an Agentic Action inside a leaf Step Run carry their actual parent Step Run, Tool identities, inputs **or** admitted protected references, results **or** errors, **and** distinguishing call evidence; report failure when required wire evidence is absent;
- check whether repeated attempts with the same Tool **and** inputs retain distinct attempt identities without claiming a second effect when its outcome is unknown; report unresolved when the supplied evidence cannot distinguish the effect;
- check whether a failed Tool call or unconfirmed effect is recorded as that outcome rather than successful completion; report failure for a contradicted success claim;
- check whether a rebuilt nested trace derives from the canonical Journal without another source of execution history; report failure when another source is claimed;
- reject an inference that a Tool call automatically creates a Workflow Step, a Conditional Step route, **or** a new Action definition; and
- check whether secret input uses a governed protected representation rather than plaintext duplication; report failure when plaintext is present.

the Evaluation **must not** edit supplied wire evidence. Missing wire evidence **or** an unperformed Evaluation is **not** a passing result.

## Summary

Serialize Project-Owned Markdown Atom Filenames

## Claim

### Prose Claim


Identified Project-owned Markdown Atom filenames other than Plan filenames governed by CA-D-469.


**every** identified Project-owned Markdown Atom filename other than a Plan filename governed by CA-D-469 **must** match `<ATOM_ID>[-<CURRENT_SCOPE>][-<TIER>][-<LABEL>][-<TARGET_SCOPE>]--<SUMMARY_SLUG>.<EXT>`. When present, the `LABEL` segment uses the Atom's effective Label: its explicit Label when present, otherwise its Form name under CA-R-2705. Normalize that token under CA-D-284; an explicit Label replaces the Form name there and does not change the Atom's Form. **every** same-identity Atom Version **must** preserve its exact assigned Atom-ID segment **in** its Carrier filename **and** serialize its retained Summary under CA-D-282. A Draft filename uses the Draft marker as its Atom-ID segment as specified by CA-D-650. An Archived predecessor uses `<canonical-ID>@<old-version>` exactly once in that segment under CA-D-289; do not append a duplicate version suffix. Existing legacy archive filenames are not normalized automatically. a replacement filename **must** contain the successor Atom ID **and** the successor's Summary Slug; a Summary Slug **must not** be edited independently of its source Summary.

## Details

The `TIER` segment follows CA-D-651. It is mandatory for numeric Tier `0` and carries the registered `SCOPE_CONTRACT` token; for other Tiers its presence and numeric encoding follow the applicable filename grammar. Omitting an optional token does not omit, default or change the mandatory stored Tier. `SCOPE_CONTRACT` is the Tier representation, not the Atom's Form or effective Label. Do not restore `PRINCIPLE` or another unregistered legacy Tier token. A legacy filename remains nonconformant until its affected Carrier and references have an explicit migration disposition; old names are not grandfathered by this rule.

This generic Project-owned Carrier rule does not replace the dedicated filename rules for an Operator-owned Project Goal. It does not invent a default numeric Tier or revive the retired named/default-Tier rules.

## Summary

Store every Atom Property in one internal location

## Claim

### Prose Claim


Atom Property representation in an Atom Markdown File Carrier.


Use YAML Frontmatter for an Atom's metadata properties. Use named Markdown
Main Content sections for `content.*` properties. Each applicable Atom Property
has one canonical internal location; its value is not duplicated between YAML
and Markdown.

This reusable Policy governs Atom representation. It does not create a Carrier
or a CARRIES fact for each property or section, and it does not change the
owning direction of an Atom-to-Atom Relation.

Qualified classifications are carried as ordinary metadata properties. For example, `Atom/(.Header.Role := Concern)` selects the Atom's `role` value, and a qualified Form selects its `form` value; neither creates a nested Role object. Use the property names and canonical value encodings registered by the applicable D policy, including CA-D-657, rather than inventing a new field from the display path.

## Semantics

YAML and Markdown are carrier locations for different Atom properties, not
alternative authorities for the same value. A section's name identifies its
`content.*` property; a metadata property remains a YAML value.

## Details

This Policy incorporates
the reusable placement boundary supported by CA-D-357 without creating a
per-field representation entity.

## Summary

Use stable headings for Atom body Properties

## Claim

### Prose Claim

Applicability: Structured Main Content of Markdown Atom carriers.

For ordinary RMED, carry one `## Summary` and one `## Claim` as sibling Properties, optionally followed by `## Semantics` and `## Details` in that order. Claim has no direct value and contains one or both `### Formal Claim` and `### Prose Claim`, with unique sibling names. Formal Claim contains a CFEL-labelled code fence; Prose Claim contains ordinary Markdown. Omit absent optional Properties. Do not duplicate Claim in frontmatter.

Map declared headings to their Property paths with a code-fence-aware outline. Only headings admitted as children by an applicable declaration are Properties. Other headings within a Markdown value, including unknown `##` headings within Prose Claim, remain part of that value and do not terminate it. A recognized Property section ends at the next recognized sibling or ancestor heading, or at the end of Main Content. Heading-like text in a fence is content. Direct value counts and dependent Property counts are independent. Retrieving a Property subtree includes its selected heading and its descendants.

Normalize recognized Property heading names to lowercase, replace spaces with underscores, and strip characters other than letters, numbers, underscore and hyphen. Reject an empty normalized key or duplicate normalized key under one parent. A flattened lookup is admissible only when unambiguous; canonical paths retain their parent chain.

Legacy layouts remain readable during migration. The existing C/A/P/O primary-content headings and their own Role-specific content rules remain applicable. A Draft may be incomplete but must satisfy the applicable complete contract before promotion.

## Summary

Use stable headings for Atom body Properties

## Claim

### Prose Claim

Applicability: Structured Main Content of Markdown Atom carriers.

For ordinary RMED, carry one `## Summary` and one `## Claim` as sibling Properties, optionally followed by `## Semantics` and `## Details` in that order. Claim has no direct value and contains one or both `### Formal Claim` and `### Prose Claim`, with unique sibling names. Formal Claim contains a CFEL-labelled code fence; Prose Claim contains ordinary Markdown. Omit absent optional Properties. Do not duplicate Claim in frontmatter.

Map declared headings to their Property paths with a code-fence-aware outline. Only headings admitted as children by an applicable declaration are Properties. Other headings within a Markdown value, including unknown `##` headings within Prose Claim, remain part of that value and do not terminate it. A recognized Property section ends at the next recognized sibling or ancestor heading, or at the end of Main Content. Heading-like text in a fence is content. Direct value counts and dependent Property counts are independent. Retrieving a Property subtree includes its selected heading and its descendants.

Normalize recognized Property heading names to lowercase, replace spaces with underscores, and strip characters other than letters, numbers, underscore and hyphen. Reject an empty normalized key or duplicate normalized key under one parent. A flattened lookup is admissible only when unambiguous; canonical paths retain their parent chain.

Legacy layouts remain readable during migration. The existing C/A/P/O primary-content headings and their own Role-specific content rules remain applicable. A Draft may be incomplete but must satisfy the applicable complete contract before promotion.

## Summary

Bind new archived Revision Markdown Carrier

## Claim

### Prose Claim


The single Markdown Archive Carrier created for an Atom Revision newly placed in Archived status.


**when** an Atom Revision newly attains its model-admitted `Archived` Status **and** no more-specific applicable Delivery mapping exists for its Artifact Type, its **`=1`** Markdown Archive Carrier **must** be classified as that Revision's Archive Carrier **and** be placed at `archive/<canonical-ID>@<version>[-<remaining-filename-components>].md`: the owning Content Role's existing `archive/` directory is retained, and the single `@<version>` marker occupies the Atom-ID segment under CA-D-283/CA-D-289. Preserve the archived Atom's numeric Version and prior Updated At; its new Archive Carrier carries `status: Archived`.

## Details

This is a binding of the existing generic Status-placement and Archive-basename rules, not a universal placement override. A more-specific admitted Delivery mapping takes precedence. It does not relocate existing historical carriers or require automatic normalization of legacy filenames.

## Summary

YAML Frontmatter encodes Atom Properties with minimal syntax

## Claim

### Prose Claim


YAML frontmatter of Markdown Atom carriers.


Encode each key once and use a YAML sequence for multiple values. Use a nonempty string for each required string; null and collections do not satisfy a scalar requirement. Integers exclude booleans.

For Markdown Atom carriers:

- Encode Role and Form as `role` and `form`, each exactly one nonempty string from the applicable domain.
- Encode identity, Version, Status, Updated At and Tier as `atom_id`, `version`, `status`, `updated_at` and `tier`. Apply their respective Property rules. An optional Label uses `label`; do not duplicate Summary or Claim in frontmatter.
- Encode Subjects under `subjects` using the Subjects serialization rule. Encode direct Node-instance Relation facts under `relations`; use each Relation's own representation and do not author inverse facts separately.
- Do not encode an Atom Author. Event authorship is governed by the Event Record model.
- Derive Target Scope Unit from the active Subject using the applicable model authority. During carrier migration, `current_scope_unit` and `claim_target_scope_unit`, if present, are legacy compatibility data; they do not establish Atom Properties or override the resolved Scope. Their retention, removal and consistency validation require the selected migration's explicit disposition. Do not infer a target from the carrier directory or use either field as an unverified fallback.
- Place a complete RMED Claim in its `## Claim` section. Its direct Markdown value may contain CFEL and need not contain prose; do not create a `Formal claim` child.

Legacy `content_role`, `type`, `subjects.governs` and `subjects.depends_on` remain readable during migration. Conflicting old and new names for the same Property are invalid in any carrier; equal pairs are readable during transition and do not create duplicate logical values. Compatibility does not make the old names canonical in the migrated model.

## Details

The remaining applicable Status, Version, identity, Tier, Label, Summary, conditional-field, Projection, Draft identity and reference constraints remain governed by their own sources. A generated Projection is not an authored source. A new field requires its own applicable authority. Summary and Claim remain body Properties, not frontmatter copies.

### Conditional fields and expansion

- A Plan's explicit `assignee` uses **<=1** String identifying an admitted Actor under the Plan Assignee encoding. `autonomous_confidence_threshold` **and** `implementation_retry_limit` use their integer encodings under the Plan confidence override and retry limit encodings. inherited values remain omitted unless explicitly selected; self-sufficiency does **not** copy them.
- `priority` follows the applicable Concern Priority authority for Concern Atoms **only**. additional Plan, Operations, proof, **or** other Type-specific fields require their applicable Delivery declarations; their occurrence **in** old Carriers does **not** admit them.
- The generated `projection` block is admitted **only** **in** a projected representation under the projection source-binding encoding, with **only** its defined `source_carrier_path` String. It is **not** an authored source Atom Property.
- A new field **or** nested key requires applicable authority that settles its canonical location, value type, cardinality, admission condition, **and** permitted values **or** reference resolution. unadmitted fields are invalid; an admitted Property with an unsettled encoding is a schema gap, **not** permission **to** guess **or** report full conformance.
- Apply explicitly governed migration exceptions **only** within their declared boundary. legacy presence alone is **not** an exception; retired fields under the canonical Property location rules remain rejected.

### Subjects-only edit-draft exception

The explicit source-pinned Subjects-only edit draft is a derived proposed next Revision of an existing Atom, not a new Atom Draft or another canonical original. It may carry `atom_id: <canonical-ID>@<proposed-version>-draft` (preferred) or the compatible `atom_id: <canonical-ID>@draft`, `status: Draft`, and a matching Draft-marker filename in the owning role's `draft/` folder while the exact canonical source remains untouched. The reviewed packet retains the canonical target/source pin and exact draft path/digest for that specific proposed edit. Approval restores the canonical ID and original Status, independently validates normalized Subjects-only materialization, and uses the existing exact predecessor archive plus N+1/actual-time update. Staging and publication require no retained Draft-history entry, `revision_lineage`, unique Draft head, origin chain or consuming successor. New-Atom Drafts and ordinary lifecycle Drafts carry exactly one Atom ID; marker and filename rules remain governed by the Draft ID marker and Draft filename marker rules. Canonical ID grammar and the normal source, schema, identity/collision, permission and exact actual-history safeguards are unchanged.

## Summary

Derive Authority and Delivery Folder Names

## Claim

### Prose Claim


The Project Authority Folder is `.caprmedio_<project name>`, without a Scope Unit ID.

For a non-root Scope Unit, derive the folder names from its ID, Label, order.number and Name:

| Scope Unit | Authority Folder name | Delivery Folder name |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Ordered | `<id>_<label>_<order>_<name>` | `<label>_<order>_<name>` |
| Unordered | `<id>_<label>_<name>` | `<label>_<name>` |

`<id>` is the stable Scope Unit ID. `<order>` is `order.number`. For an Unordered unit, omit the order segment and its separator. When Label is absent, omit its segment and separator.

Place each non-root folder under its respective parent's folder. Do not maintain the derived folder paths as independent values in Scope Unit Declarations.

Derived paths are readability and placement values, not another structural source. Conflicting derivations remain unresolved and are reported; do not automatically choose a new Name, parent, number or binding. Do not author Structural Level or Structural Coordinate.

## Summary

Validate replacement Event schema encoding

## Claim

### Prose Claim


the Main Content of the selected schema-version `3` replacement Journal Event Carrier.


the Main Content of the selected schema-version `3` replacement Journal Event Carrier **must** support evaluation of CA-D-435-PROJECT_CONFIGURATION-DELIVERY--serialize-atom-replacement-event-references without treating Project conformance as storage integrity.

## Cases

- case 1: encode a completed File Carrier `MOVE` Event Record with paired string predecessor **and** array-of-string successor fields; preserve the supplied successor order.
- case 2: keep that envelope valid **and** vary the observed IDs: canonical, legacy, nonconforming, duplicate, self-referencing, **or** an empty successor array. also vary the result filename **or** archive placement independently of the safe Event path encoding.
- case 3: omit **only** one paired field, supply null **or** the wrong storage type, use a schema **or** Event kind that does **not** define the pair, **or** change the payload **without** updating its digest.
- case 4: replay an identical sealed Event Record; **then** submit a different payload under the same Event identity.
- case 5: validate an ordinary historical Event Record without replacement fields.

## Acceptance

the Main Content evaluation **must** report that:

- cases 1 **and** 2 remain recordable with the supplied values unchanged. case 2 **may** fail CA-E-462-CORE_META_MODEL-POLICY--validate-atom-replacement-event-evidence independently; its conformance verdict **must not** prevent recording under CA-R-1491-CORE_META_MODEL-RULE--keep-project-validation-out-of-journal-admission.
- case 3 fails the selected encoding **or** integrity check without changing accepted history.
- the identical replay reuses the existing receipt without a duplicate record; an identity collision with a different payload fails without overwriting history.
- case 5 retains its selected historical schema. passing this Evaluation does **not** prove active successors, exact archive preservation, valid Project identifiers, valid placement, **or** a correctly performed replacement.

## Summary

Serialize Atom replacement event references

## Claim

### Prose Claim


actual Atom replacement references supplied to the Main Content of a Journal Carrier.


the Main Content of a Journal Carrier **must** preserve the actually supplied predecessor **and** successor Atom references of a replacement observation, including `predecessor_atom_id` **and** `successor_atom_ids` **when** supplied.

- preserve reference values **and** array order as data through safe encoding. array order does **not** establish priority **or** execution order.
- do **not** look up an earlier Journal Event Record, require a predecessor chain, compute a digest, validate the replacement **or** fabricate a baseline **to** append these observations.
- absence of replacement references does **not** establish whether the action was a replacement. do **not** infer missing identities, successors **or** historical facts.
- existing encoded Event Record representations remain readable **without** rewriting their fields, selected representation **or** observed values. legacy **or** nonconforming values remain observations, **not** certified replacements.
- actual source replacement, exact predecessor history **and** successor correctness remain independently governed by CA-R-807 **and** CA-E-462. Journal Carrier append **or** read grants no source-effect permission **and** proves none of those conditions.

## Summary

Bind instance variables

## Claim

### Prose Claim


- `Kind//` selects existing instances of Kind and its narrower kinds.
- `Kind//{:n}` applies the existing cardinality to the selected logical instances within the Project context. Resolve the complete selection and count each instance once across repeated references or Carrier representations. An unresolved population is an error.
- `Kind//$x` ranges over the selected instances. Each constraint must hold for every matching binding. Repeated `$x` references in one Claim block identify the same instance within each binding.
- `in` and `not in` test an instance's identity against a selected instance set. `=` and `!=` compare bound instance references by identity; they do not test kind membership or broadcast a scalar comparison over a set.
- `Kind//$x.p` selects and binds an instance and reads its Property `p`. `$x.p` reads that same bound instance's Property.
- In an IF condition, `Kind//$c ((R)) Kind//$p` tests a link that already exists, including a legitimately derived inverse. It is not an endpoint signature and does not create a link.
- Evaluate the condition for candidate bindings. Its THEN conclusion applies only to bindings for which that link exists; it does not require links between every candidate pair.
- Endpoint counts aggregate matching links per endpoint; they do not require a link between every pair of bindings.
- Binding selects existing instances. It does not create an instance named `$x` or assign a value imperatively. A bare qualified address refers to its declared target.

## Details

```CFEL
Kind//$x
```

This binds one existing selected instance.

In one CFEL Formal Claim fence, the full-line comments `# model` and `# instances` distinguish MODEL constraints from instance constraints. When both are present, write `# model` first. These comments are not operators, Properties, or values. Named MODEL addresses such as `Relation//NAME` and `Operator//NAME` retain their declared identity; a Relation descriptor variable in the MODEL group does not make it a runtime instance constraint.

In the MODEL group, `IF $x in (selection) THEN (conclusion)` binds an unbound `$x` over the selected MODEL entities. If `$x` is already bound, the membership test filters that same binding. References to `$x` throughout the parenthesized conclusion use the same binding; the conclusion may contain nested conditions and semicolon-separated statements. This does not create a MODEL entity or introduce a FOR operator.

`KindSelection//$x` binds existing members of the selected logical instance population. The receiver may be a named Kind or a union Kind selection: `(in (Action, Workflow))//$selected` keeps the Action-or-Workflow population and binds its matching members. An existing filter follows the explicit binder without changing its matching population, as in `Event Record//$event_record(.object_output{=1}, .object_output.id = $projection.ID)`. In an aggregate such as `MAX(Event Record//$event_record(.object_output{=1}).happened_at)`, the argument remains the complete filtered population; inserting the binder does not turn the aggregate into one calculation per selected row.

`Kind//$x{:n}` constrains the count of the entire selected logical population in its Project context, not a count of one already-bound row. ## Summary

Write Subject Expressions with Bearer and Value Qualification

## Claim

### Prose Claim

Applicability: authoring one Subject expression.

Use the declared Primary Entity and Property paths. `/` selects a narrower Primary Entity; `//` selects a named instance of a declared kind; `.` addresses a declared Property of its bearer. An unchanged inherited Property resolves to its existing declaration. A heading alone does not declare a Property.

Count direct values independently of child Properties. YAML null and empty strings are direct values; state necessary value restrictions through the Format or applicable prose. Use prose when formal machinery is unnecessary. Write a Property value constraint as `property: [format]{:count}`. Use `.*` for immediate child names and `.**` for recursive child names; constrain child values separately. Use `{:n}`, `{:n+}`, and `{:n..m}` for exact, lower-bounded, and inclusive bounded allowed counts. Use `{=n}` for a condition and `{==n}` for setting a count.

Write a named Relation object as `Relation//NAME` and its actual use as `Source {:left}((NAME)){:right} Target`, with each endpoint count optional. A Relation Declaration can state both intrinsic endpoint bounds. A Node-specific Claim addresses its active Node and its own bound. Reversing a written view swaps the bounds; it does not grant opposite-view permission, which must be declared separately. Resolve aliases as typed Relation instances and write a counterpart as `<-->`. Short operators remain valid where declared.

Use `:` for allowed values, `=` for a condition, `==` for setting a value, and `:=` for allowed value and condition in a Subject. Separate complete expressions with semicolons. Use bare Entity references without an `@` reference marker.

An ordinary RMED Claim is a zero-direct-value group with one or both declared Formal Claim and Prose Claim children. Formal Claim contains a CFEL-labelled fence; Prose Claim contains ordinary Markdown.

## Summary

Reject Invalid Subject Expressions

## Claim

### Prose Claim


Entity Expressions evaluated for invalid component handling.


Under A1296, count an omitted property as zero values, a scalar null as one value, and an empty string as one value. Check the parsed value against the declared Format and applicable prose conditions separately. Do not pass a required string merely because a null satisfies the count; do not reject an empty string solely because it is empty unless the applicable rules require substantive/nonempty content.

For the Entity format check under CA-A-1285, check string-valued content and the admitted notation. Do not fail that format check solely because a defining Atom introduces a new governed entity. Target authority and explicit existing-kind reference resolution are separate semantic checks, not consequences of the string Format.

Under CA-A-1283, admit subjects{0} with one governs reference and zero or more dependencies; reject a direct subjects scalar without rejecting its declared children. Require direct prose for claim{1} even when formal_claim{0..1} is present. For property[string]{2}, require two string values under one key; repeated sibling YAML keys do not satisfy cardinality. Do not treat a sequence as one list-formatted value or count child keys as direct parent values.

Accept Package/Project Implementation as the parentless root Package and each Module only when it belongs to exactly one Package; reject the superseded root-under-Implementation and independent-Module cases.

For cardinality under CA-A-1280, accept `{0}`, `{1}`, `{3}`, `{0+}`, `{1+}`, `{2+}`, `{0..1}` and `{2..5}` with their declared counts. Reject negative or fractional bounds, an empty `{}`, a missing range bound such as `{2..}`, repeated plus signs such as `{1++}`, and an inverted range such as `{5..2}`. A Step count of zero fails `Step {:1}+>{:1+} Workflow`; zero Substeps is admitted by `Sub-step {:1}+>{:0+} Step`. A containment count must not be read as inheritance or as changing the exactly-one immediate-whole rule.

the Evaluation **must** reject an Entity Expression **if**

- `/` does **not** express the approved broader-to-narrower Entity Path profile,
- `//` does **not** occur exactly between an Entity kind component and a following named instance component, or the entire path fails to resolve to exactly one canonical Entity Target that already exists or is explicitly introduced by applicable defining authority under CA-R-1194 and CA-R-1321,
- `.` does **not** encode **`=1`** valid bearer edge from the following Property occurrence **to** the immediately preceding bearer occurrence,
- `:` does **not** express an admitted allowed value of its preceding X under CA-R-1245-CORE_META_MODEL-RULE--qualify-allowed-values-with-colon,
- `.Header.Form` is interpreted as a primary Entity **or** as a Property subtype of Atom instead of as a Property relative to Atom,
- `Atom/(.Header.Form: Method)` is used as syntax-only evidence that Method is admitted as a Form,
- superseded bare `X/Y: Z` qualification spelling is used in this proposal,
- `>|` or `|<` is interpreted as membership through IS_CLASSIFIED_BY instead of the HAS_CLASSIFICATION axis,
- `*` ranges beyond admitted Atom Status values in a Status classification,
- `+>` and `<+` are interpreted as different containment facts, their direction is swapped, **or** either is used as inheritance,
- Current fails to exclude Draft and Archived within the admitted Atom Status values,
- a Relation count is interpreted as only an outgoing count despite its two slots, a post-operator slot is treated as outgoing rather than reverse, **or** equivalent forward and reverse writings are given different constraints,
- allowed-value admission is treated as assignment **to** a particular Property occurrence **or** as determining its cardinality,
- a Property occurrence lacks **`=1`** immediate bearer,
- a reusable Term is rejected **only** for changing ordinal position,
- a Governed Term begins with a lowercase letter,
- an ordinary named component other than the RHS instance name following `//` fails **to** resolve **to** a Term under CA-R-1321-CORE_META_MODEL--define-subject-expression,
- an ordinary General Term is substituted for a required Term reference,
- a name uses an unescaped reserved operator character as literal text, or has an unmatched final backslash,
- a structural containment edge through `+>` or `<+` is used as an inheritance route,
- a qualified reference fails to resolve to its intended already declared Entity,
- a complete composite Entity Expression is classified as one Term,
- **or** a registered CCE Operator is redefined as a Governed Term **or** Scope Unit Name.

For example, in `Kind//Instance Name`, the RHS identifies the named instance and is not automatically a Term; require the complete path to resolve to exactly one canonical target that already exists or is explicitly introduced by applicable defining authority. References must resolve to their intended declared targets. Recognizing `//` alone does not establish or admit an INSTANCE_OF graph fact. Do not reject or accept the name by an Atom-ID pattern; its source/name authority and exact-target resolution govern.

## Details

### Term-component cases

`Atom.Header.Status: Active` **must** pass the component check **only when** its named lexical components **and** exact qualified target are admitted. `/`, `.`, **and** `:` contribute no Term nodes. `Atom/(.Header.Role := Plan)/(.Header.Form := Epic).Header.Status` **must** pass only when its components and qualified target are admitted; its syntax alone does not admit values or a target. An unadmitted Role or Form value **must** fail. an unresolved ordinary named component **must** fail the source-reference check; the diagnostic **must** preserve the unresolved reference **without** supplying an invented definition. a complete composite path **must not** be admitted as **`=1`** Term merely because it resolves **to** **`=1`** Entity Target.

Use an admitted Method Atom whose actual GOVERNS target is `Atom.Content`; retain the fixture's source Atom and exact Revision. Check that complete target against its governing authority separately from component-Term meaning. The Method Content Role does not create a Method Subject root or determine the target's category. A Scope Unit, folder, or Carrier spelling cannot substitute for the target binding.

The schematic expression `Atom/(.Header.Form: Method)` denotes an Atom qualified by its own Form Property value; the result is narrower than Atom and inherits applicable Atom features and constraints. `.Header.Form` is relative to Atom, not a primary Entity or a Property subtype of Atom. `Atom/(.Header.Role: Method)` is the concrete canonical example because Method is already a Role; its notation alone does not admit Method as a Form. Neither form creates an intermediate Entity kind, a named instance, or membership through IS_CLASSIFIED_BY. ### Containment alternatives

In the complete declared containment structure, each branch is an allowed option. `X <+ Y` requires a contained Y instance to belong to exactly one immediate whole instance of the permitted kind.
